prompt.text:
Make a 30-second vertical motion-graphics explainer (1080×1920, 30 fps) on how GPS finds your phone.

Use `script.md` for the exact on-screen text and `sources/` for the facts. No voiceover. For sound, use only the music bed and sound effects in `benchmarks/shared/audio/`. Go for a clean, modern, flat style with animated diagrams.

revision_prompt.text: Revise only the trilateration scene (script scene 5). Make its satellite and sphere diagram 20% larger, change that scene's accent color to #00C2A8, and change its first line to the exact text "One signal: you're somewhere on this sphere." Leave every other scene, the total length and the audio unchanged.

assumptions: Split script scene 5 into two plan scenes (scene_5: first line, 2.4 s; scene_6: lines 2-3, 3.6 s) because a director scene only has title+subtitle entering together; the diagram plate is continuous across the cut. The revision therefore touches both plan scenes.

Animated diagrams were made as text-free procedural plates (Pillow, tools/make_plates.py in the private workspace), imported with import-video and approved as CC0 agent-original assets; the build has no native diagram primitives.

Scene durations were chosen on the 100 BPM beat grid (cuts at multiples of 18 frames): 90,126,108,162,72+108,126,108 frames; numbers are shown as static animated labels rather than counters because the counter primitive cannot fit 'within 4.9 m (16 ft)' on one unwrapped line.
Font: Segoe UI Semibold from the Windows system, supplied via --font-dir (copy in the ignored workspace); the preview renderer uses one face for title and subtitle.

Research: every scene cites a ledger claim with a supporting GPS.gov excerpt; the textbook parts of scenes 3-5 are recorded as uncertainty, not as sourced facts. QA status needs_review (semantic claim review) is expected.

20% larger diagram implemented by re-rendering the scene-5 plates with the diagram scaled 1.2x about its own centre and accent #00C2A8, applied via typed set_asset; set_visual_zoom would scale about the canvas centre and push the diagram out of frame, and no typed op recolours content inside a plate.

agent_checks.item: Every line in script.md appears exactly once, spelled exactly, fully readable (not clipped, not covered, on screen >= 1.5 s)
agent_checks.evidence: Draft runs/b1-gps/v3.motion.json text elements compared programmatically with the 15 quoted strings in script.md: each occurs exactly once, no extras. Fully opaque windows: shortest is scene_5 'One distance: you're somewhere on a sphere' frames 500-557 (1.93 s; the fade-in starts at frame 486); the next shortest is scene_1, frames 18-89 (2.37 s). The renderer raises an error on any text overflow, and the render passed. Text sits at z=2 above plates in the lower third (y>=1190), which plates never draw into. Frames 420 and 640 checked visually: fully legible, not clipped. Subtitles are 41 px (the compiler's fixed size): readable at full resolution but small on a phone.

agent_checks.item: No on-screen text or numbers that are not in script.md
agent_checks.evidence: Diagram plates are procedurally drawn and contain no glyphs (tools/make_plates.py draws only shapes). 2-fps contact sheet of v3 (60 frames) checked: the only text is script lines. Revised v5 adds only the line REVISION.md requires ('One signal: you're somewhere on this sphere.'), which replaces the scene 5 first line.

agent_checks.item: Scene 5 visibly shows the step from one sphere to an intersection of several
agent_checks.evidence: Frame 530 (plan scene_5): one range sphere around a single satellite, with a ghost pin sliding over its surface. Frame 640 (plan scene_6): three spheres intersect, the pin locks at the intersection, and a fourth satellite's wavefront plus a clock badge collapse the uncertainty blob. The same holds in v5 (teal, 1.2x).

agent_checks.item: Only the shared music and SFX files are used; the music fades in and out, with no clipping (true peak <= -1 dBTP)
agent_checks.evidence: Audio assets are byte copies of benchmarks/shared/audio/*.wav (music bed + whoosh-short/long, pop, tick, impact, riser), hashed in runs/b1-gps/assets.json. Soundtrack: -3 dB with a 24-frame fade-in and a 54-frame fade-out. Mean volume: 0-0.1 s -55.3 dB, 2-3 s -22.1 dB, 29.9-30 s -52.5 dB. ebur128 on both v3 and v5: I = -20.3 LUFS, true peak -4.2 dBTP.

agent_checks.item: No blank, black or frozen frames outside intended holds
agent_checks.evidence: ffmpeg blackdetect=d=0.25:pix_th=0.05 and freezedetect=n=0.001:d=1 (bench settings) report 0 black and 0 frozen segments on both v3 and v5. An earlier internal draft (v2) had two low-motion holds (13.2-15.9 s, 17.2-18.6 s); these were fixed before delivery by adding hold motion. Scene starts: frame 0 shows the phone at 35% opacity and frame 90 shows Earth at 45% scale, so no empty frames.

agent_checks.item: Revision: only scene 5 changed. Other scenes are frame-identical (or hash-identical modules) to the draft.
agent_checks.evidence: Comparing v3-scenes/scene-modules.json with v5-scenes/scene-modules.json: plan scenes 1-4, 7 and 8 have identical PNG frame-tree SHA-256, scene mix WAV SHA-256 and scene MP4 SHA-256. Only scene_5 and scene_6 (together script scene 5) differ. Total length is 900 frames / 30.000 s in both. Scene audio hashes are identical for all 8 scenes. Caveat: sceneInputSha256 differs for every scene because set_asset adds to the spec-wide asset list, so revise-production could not reuse the cache (see notes).

notes: Drafts: v1 and v2 were internal iterations (v2 fixed near-empty first frames and raised music 3 dB; v3 added hold motion after freezedetect flagged 2 low-motion holds). Revision gap: revise-production v3->v4 failed with 'no compatible module for scene scene_1' because set_asset with a new asset record changes spec.assets, which is part of every scene's sceneInputSha256; the revision was completed with revise-scene x2 + render-scenes (all 8) + assemble-scenes + qa + make-review-site + make-editor-delivery, and unchanged scenes were proven frame/audio/MP4 hash-identical to the draft. Editor delivery prepared 0 Adobe adapters. Setup note: bench.py warned that PATH motion-engine is 0.63.1; all work used the checkout's .venv 0.68.0.

owner_review.comment: Really good motion graphics. First benchmark baseline, published so users can watch the engine grow.
